heroHeadline: EU Unanimously Approves Settler Sanctions as IDF Drone Kills IED Operative in Khan Younis — Cemetery Exhumation Shocks International Community
heroSubtitle: In a significant diplomatic shift on May 11, 2026, all 27 EU foreign ministers unanimously approved sanctions against violent Israeli settlers and Hamas leaders — the first such package in 21 months, enabled by Hungary's new government lifting its longstanding veto. Seven settlers and settler organizations were blacklisted with asset freezes and travel bans; proposals to sanction ministers Ben-Gvir and Smotrich were dropped. Separately, the IDF Kfir Brigade released drone footage of a strike on a Palestinian operative planting an IED in the Khan Younis area of southern Gaza under the October 2025 ceasefire, bringing the cumulative Palestinian death toll since the ceasefire to approximately 875+. Meanwhile, settlers in the West Bank forced a Palestinian family to exhume and rebury their 80-year-old father's body from a cemetery near the re-established Sa-Nur settlement, with Israeli soldiers present but not intervening — drawing UN condemnation as an example of 'growing dehumanization.' Spanish-Palestinian flotilla activist Saif Abukeshek returned to Barcelona after six days in Israeli custody following the Global Sumud Flotilla interception. The Gaza war death toll since October 7, 2023 stands at 72,673+ documented, with the true toll with indirect deaths estimated to exceed 90,000–100,000.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
